 Two recalls announced October 22 involve children’s products that could cause serious injuries or death.
 HIGH CHAIR RECALL 
 Costway is recalling about 3,332 convertible high chairs because they do not contain the passive restraint system required under the federal high-chair safety standard.
 A child can slip through the opening between the feeding tray and seat, potentially becoming trapped or falling. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
 The chairs convert into table-and-chair sets and were sold in several colors. They were available at Walmart and Target stores nationwide and through Costway.com from May 2023 through July 2026 for between $84 and $100. Consumers should stop using the chairs and contact Costway for a free replacement. Customers must provide a receipt or product photograph and use a prepaid shipping label to return the recalled chair.
 LED FINGER LIGHT RECALL 
 Bamamon is recalling about 6,533 LED projecting finger light toys because their button-cell battery compartments can be opened easily by children.
 Swallowed button batteries can cause internal chemical burns, serious injuries or death. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
 The toys were sold in 32-piece packages on Amazon from March 2025 through August 2026 for approximately $13 to $14. Consumers should stop using the toys and contact Bamamon for a refund.
 Customers will be asked to send the company a photograph showing that the products were properly discarded. The batteries should be handled according to local hazardous-waste procedures.
